reviewer: independent-agent (adversarial, Claude Code subagent; not the r24 producer)
method: Read-only. No FormSeed MCP calls, locks, renders, approvals or git operations; this file is the only write. I did not open the private reference photo. Steps: (1) viewed the r24 production pass-2 contact sheet; (2) computed my own pixel diff of r23 (run-drTFYM) against r24 (run-b7Bmu0) across all 13 production views with numpy (per-pixel max RGBA delta, threshold 8, bbox, alpha-change count); (3) downscaled az-315, ortho front and az-0 to 256 px over a grey background to judge native size; (4) viewed the r24 close-ups polsten-oblique-close, opaque flange-left-side, bolt-probe-oblique, bolt-probe-profile, and the same-camera r23->r24 pairs polsten-seat-side and polsten-seat-top, plus report.json; (5) parsed r24-request.json and checked bolt geometry against the flange profile in build-r24.json (ring-face x, bolt-circle radius, radial fit and floor-clip clearance), the operation order (bolts created and joined after the floor-clip boolean) and set_parent P06 -> M.turret; (6) read the producer record, native isolation summary, dimensions24.json header, the r22 independent review, the r23 producer record and the rubric. I did not run the deterministic evaluator. I did not re-verify the native-isolation receipt, the validation report or the dimension report beyond reading the hash-bound summaries.

evidenceInspected.sha256: not individually hashed; diff results in changeConfinement

changeConfinement.method: My own numpy per-pixel max RGBA delta of r23 production pass-2 (run-drTFYM) against r24 (run-b7Bmu0), threshold 8, plus the producer's same-camera close-up report and native isolation summary.
changeConfinement.closeups: In the producer's same-camera r23->r24 pairs, the changed pixels in polsten-seat-side and polsten-seat-top are only small blocks on the ring face where the bolt heads now sit. The boss, collar, ball, kink apex and inboard shard are pixel-identical by eye. The report's maximum changedFraction is 0.0059, and flange-side, turret-front-quarter and bolt-probe-profile report 0.0.
changeConfinement.geometry: r24-request.json differs from r23 only in the bolt mesh, which is now a separate closed shell created and joined after the floor-clip boolean, and in the steel face slot. The other P06 operations, including set_parent P06 -> M.turret, are unchanged. build-r24.py asserts that the bolts keep the same y/z positions as r23 and that only the rear face moved onto the ring face. Native isolation reports 150/151 objects identical to r23, P09 content identical, and only P06 changed. Triangles 49,838 -> 49,982 (+144 = 12 x 12).
changeConfinement.verdict: Confined. No pixel change appears outside the Polsten ring in any of the 13 production views, and no alpha (silhouette) change appears anywhere. Geometry and native evidence agree that only the P06 bolt heads changed. I found no evidence of any change other than the directed bolt restore.

boltVerification.count: 12. The request has 96 vertices and 72 faces (12 closed boxes). I counted about 12 heads around the ring in polsten-oblique-close, with one or two partly occluded by the ball and barrel.
boltVerification.seating: Seated, not floating and not embedded. The ring face lies at world x 1.116, the flange profile point x -0.004 offset by 1.12, since the collar front at X_SPLIT 0.025 maps to the flange max x of 1.145. Bolt shells span x 1.116 to 1.130, so the rear face is coplanar with the ring face and the heads stand 14 mm proud. All 12 bolt centres lie at radius 0.2003 to 0.2004 from the axis. With a half-diagonal of 0.0184, the heads span r 0.182 to 0.219, inside the ring face annulus r 0.16174 to 0.239. The lowest bolt vertex is at z 0.1405, well clear of the floor clip at z <= 0.045. Visually, the heads sit on the dark ring face with no gap and no burial in flange-left-side, polsten-oblique-close, polsten-seat-side, polsten-seat-top and bolt-probe-oblique.
boltVerification.caveat: bolt-probe-profile.png shows only flat olive planes, so it is uninformative about the bolts. It neither supports nor contradicts seating. Seating rests on the other close-ups and the coordinates. The rear bolt faces are coplanar with the ring face (zero-thickness contact, separate shells joined into one object). They are hidden, so I see no rendering risk, but the bolts are not welded.

At 256 px, the dark Polsten ring is a legible dark donut in ortho front and a small dark mark in az-0 and az-315. The bolts restore the detail George asked for at close range and do not alter native-size identity.

coreCategoryObjections.resolutionObservation: George explicitly accepted the softened kink. r24 has zero alpha changes against r23 in all 13 views, and the major contours are unchanged at gameplay scale. The facets show only at close range.

coreCategoryObjections.strongestReasonBelowThree: Carried from r22: the fixed flange was parented to the articulated ball, and there is no posed evidence. New for r24: the bolts could be floating, buried or clipped by the floor boolean, as happened in r23. Also carried: the inboard wedge shard at the spot-face.
coreCategoryObjections.resolutionObservation: From r23 onward, P06 (ring, bolts, collar) is parented to M.turret and P09 moves alone, which resolves the parenting. Bolts are created after the floor clip, with their rear faces exactly on the ring face (x 1.116), radially inside the ring annulus and above the clip plane (min z 0.1405 against 0.045). The close-ups show them seated with no gap. The wedge shard is unchanged and was deliberately not selected by George; it is a known residual, not a regression. Posed ball evidence is still absent, but no articulation limits are declared, so it is a coverage gap for a later animation gate, not a static-structure defect.
